historical_references.reference:
Ibn Khaldun describes 'Abd al-Haqq ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-'Umari as the ruler of the Banu Afham in his 'The Muqaddimah'. He reigned from 1295 to 1310 AD in Al-Andalus (Iberian Peninsula), and is known for his successful military campaigns against the Castilians and his efforts to rebuild the Almohad Caliphate.
Reference: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, pp. 364-365.

The Banu Afham was a Berber dynasty that ruled in the Maghreb region from 1146 to 1229 AD. They were the successors of the Almoravids and are known for their patronage of Islamic learning and culture, as well as their military successes against Christian invaders. The name 'Afham' is derived from the Berber word 'ifham', which means 'understanding'.
Reference: Perez-Ruiz, Javier, The Banu Ghaniya and the Mediterranean World in the Thirteenth Century, pp. 13-14.
